(3) Party Mode now carries delta_se_s and a CI (races independent); fixed a toFixed(null) crash on 42 rows. Feature tests 29 pass; full vitest 828 pass / 2 pre-existing fail; typecheck and lint clean. OWNER DECISIONS PENDING: (a) the season interval narrows ~4x; the agent's own cross-check found the spread of a team's race estimates gives SD/sqrt(k) ~3x LARGER than the shipped SE in all 81 cells, i.e. the per-race SEs look understated: the narrower interval is a lower bound and the spread-based one is the more honest, but it was not built; (b) a 'not distinguishable' label would relabel 478 race-grain rows and 6 season cells; (c) the season 'Races' column now counts only races with an estimate (22 cells change, e.g. 2018 Mercedes 21 -> 18). Not committed. (1) Season SE = sqrt(max(VAR_SAMP(p), mean(se^2))/k), CI = mean +/- t_97.5(k-1) SE, NULL below k=3; leave-one-race-out coverage (a) 45% vs (c) 93%; top-two separated in 3 of 8 seasons under (c) vs 5 of 8 under the shipped lower bound. (2) Party Mode: party needs delta < -0.15 and CI wholly below 0; race needs delta > 0.15 and CI wholly above 0; else 'no clear gap'; NULL delta -> no label; 'balanced' retired (374 of 378 balanced rows have CIs reaching outside +/-0.15 s). Season delta must be AVG(q - r) over races with both values (the old AVG(q) - AVG(r) shifts up to 0.071 s). (3) Races = k with a tooltip. Card sample size n = {count: k, unit: 'races'}; the card interval kind needs a t-interval (ci_t_95) or ci_normal_95. 2026-11-08 lane M (sonnet): built as ruled. Mercedes 2020 race k=16 mean -1.273324114303026, SE 0.10038245862558223, CI [-1.4873,-1.0594] with t(15)=2.1314, Obs 1440, asserted to 12 dp. Race-grain labels party 364 / race 382 / no clear gap 856 / no delta 42; season grain 81 cells: party 27, race 20, no clear gap 34. Feature tests 33 pass; full vitest 874 pass / 2 pre-existing fail; typecheck and eslint clean on both folders (full pnpm lint not run). DIFFERENCES FROM SPEC: Races column tooltip is a footnote under the season table with a title attribute (RankedTable headers are plain strings; ui/ not touched); t975 returns null below df 2; the t table was generated from scipy to 4 dp but only spot-checked (df 2, 8, 15, 20, 22, 60). decisions.question: Who pays for the answers? A: the project holds one API key behind a proxy, with a per-visitor daily limit. B: each visitor brings their own key, nothing is stored server-side. C: A for a small free quota, then B.
decisions.context: A is the easiest for a fan but costs the project money and needs rate limiting and abuse handling. B costs nothing and has no abuse surface, but most casual fans will not have a key. C builds both paths. The CSP, App Check and the proxy design differ between A and B, so AI-06 cannot start before this is ruled. AI-07 measures cost per answer before AI-06 is needed, so the cap can be set from data. Recommendation revised 2026-10-15 from C to A for v1: C builds two paths before there is any usage data.
decisions.recommendation: A for v1, with a per-visitor daily limit and a hard daily spend cap sized from AI-07's cost per answer; add B later only if the cap binds.
decisions.resolution: Cloudflare Workers AI, on the account's free allowance (about 10,000 neurons a day) for now. The proxy is a Cloudflare Worker that calls Workers AI; the key/binding lives in the Worker, never the browser bundle. Firebase Hosting stays; the Worker is the only thing that touches the model API. Nothing else is decided (no paid tier, no bring-your-own-key path).

decisions.question: Which model and tool shape does the assistant launch with?
decisions.context: The prototype's model (gpt-oss-20b, 20,480-token window) cannot hold the one-tool plan AI-04 assumed, and the plan named Llama 3.3 70B. The prototype also let the model write its own SQL, which has no sample size and cannot be graded.
decisions.recommendation: gpt-oss-20b on Workers AI (and locally through Ollama for development); seven tools; a structured query builder instead of model-written SQL.
decisions.resolution: Owner ruling 2026-10-22. Model: gpt-oss-20b, mixture-of-experts, 20,480-token window, budget split in the AI-04 and AI-07 docs. Tools: fact cards (get_fact_cards), bounded query builder (query_data), exact-code lookup (list_values), lap-time comparison (compare_lap_times), charts (make_chart), page explainer (explain_page), navigation (navigate). No model-written SQL in v1. Worker fixes model, prompt, tool set and output cap server-side; browser-sent tools, max_tokens and reasoning are ignored.

decisions.question: May the assistant quote numbers from the query builder, which carry a sample size but no uncertainty interval?
decisions.context: Fact cards carry value, n, interval and source. Query-builder results carry n per row and no interval. Without this ruling the query builder cannot answer most open questions.
decisions.recommendation: Yes, labelled as plain counts or averages, with n on every row.
decisions.resolution: Owner ruling 2026-10-22: yes. Query-builder results are labelled computed_not_card and the answer must state they are plain counts or averages. Fact cards remain the only source for rated or modelled numbers.

decisions.question: What is the launch cost and access limit? A: a paid plan with a hard daily spend cap. B: free allowance only. C: serve from the owner's machine through a tunnel.
decisions.context: Owner deferred this 2026-10-22: decide once the assistant works well. Until then the Worker carries a low placeholder daily cap (about 1 USD of usage) and a per-visitor limit, so testing cannot run up a bill. Free allowance is about 10,000 neurons a day, roughly 20-30 answers for the whole site at about 460 neurons each.
decisions.recommendation: Decide at launch readiness, from AI-07's measured cost per answer. Paid plan with the Worker's counter as the real cap is the working assumption.
decisions.resolution: Owner ruling 2026-10-23: B for now (free allowance only). Owner's words earlier: "get this working properly before heading into monetisation". Mapping to B is now confirmed. W1 stays open: the placeholder daily cap is still required until AI-12 lands.

watch_vocabulary.ship-blocker: Publishing or shipping without this breaks something users see. `board.py --ship` exits 1 while one is open.
watch_vocabulary.hazard: A standing trap that damages tracked files or results if someone does the obvious thing. Read before running anything nearby.
watch_vocabulary.uncommitted: Verified work that lives only in the working tree. Committing is the user's call.
watch_vocabulary.unreviewed: Changes in the working tree that no orchestrator has read or tested. Not to be built on until reviewed.
watch_vocabulary.unverified: A claim or code path that was run in one place only (dev but not CI, agent report but not re-run).
watch_vocabulary.stale-artifact: A built or generated thing that no longer matches the source it came from until it is rebuilt.
watch_vocabulary.pending-ruling: A question for the human that is not (yet) a blocking FD: it changes a note, a value or a scope, not an item's ability to run.
watch_vocabulary.gate-gap: A guard that does not guard: it errors, skips files silently, or cannot fail.
watch_vocabulary.debt: Known, documented, deliberately left. Each needs an owner eventually.

watch_model_vocabulary.haiku: Maps to haiku-4-5. A binary check, or recording a resolution the evidence or the user has already settled: is it committed, did the named tests pass on the rebuild, write down the accept. The output has a mechanical check (a test result, a file list, git log).
watch_model_vocabulary.sonnet: Maps to sonnet-5. The fix or the options are written down in the rule: pick between two named options, run a named rebuild or export and check the pages, review a diff, reconcile counts, reword text to a meaning already settled.
watch_model_vocabulary.opus: Maps to opus-5 (fable-5.1 if the rule turns into a new estimator). Rules on a trade-off, designs the fix, audits a decision, or turns a measurement into a claim: label-moving changes, leakage boundaries, gate runs before a promotion.
